newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Futures-related buying of South African shares helped industrial stocks retrace the bulk of their losses on Tuesday to end only a touch weaker.

But gold shares were unable to shake the negative effects of bullion which fell to three-year lows in afternoon trade. Stocks shrugged off a weaker rand, dragging the gold index to its lowest close in 11 months.
"The gold price is looking really shoddy and it is taking shares down with it," a dealer said.
"Technically it (bullion) looks like it is breaking down further, which spells further weakness for shares tomorrow (Wednesday)."
The gold index fell 31 points or 2.03 percent to 1,492.4 -- its weakest finish since January 4 when it ended at 1,480.2.
Amongst gold shares Kloof shed 3.4 percent or 125 cents to 36.10 rand, Dries lost almost five percent or 250 cents to 50.50 rand and Gold Fields dropped 75 cents to 134 rand.
At 1500 GMT bullion was trading at $367.40 breaking through support at $368. It was set at $369 an ounce in London, its lowest fixing since November 3, 1993.
Dealers said the turnaround in industrial shares during the afternoon took the market by surprise as sentiment remained poor on the rand which weakened again to below the 4.65 level on the dollar.
"Futures guys just suddenly came in when contracts started trading at a wide enough premium to spot. They started buying up equities and selling futures which lifted the stocks," a trader said.
Industrial shares had spent most of the day weak on offshore and local selling with the index down over 30 points at its weakest levels.
At the close the index was only 1.1 points softer at 7,991.7. Amongst shares SAB was 100 cents softer at 116 rand, Absa up 50 cents at 24.75 rand and Sasol 75 cents better at 57.50 rand.
Traders said futures players, who were seen short of stock, were expected to boost industrial shares again on Wednesday.
On the futures market December industrial contracts were last firmer at 7,765/80 from 7,738 lifting similar-dated all-share contracts to 6,175/95 from 6,125 on Monday.
Golds remained weak on bullion to trade at 1,025/39 from 1,064 settlement.
